
spec
  
  spec-writer · opus
  
  • What change would you like to make?
  
  > Add a top-level `--version` flag (with a `-V` short alias) to the `imp` CLI
    that prints the installed imp version and exits 0, without requiring a
    subcommand. Read the version from the installed package metadata
    (importlib.metadata) so it stays in sync with pyproject.toml.
  
  • Let me explore the CLI structure before proposing a design.
  
    ToolSearch · 2 calls · 2s
  
  • Let me explore the CLI structure.
  
    grep · glob · 2 calls · 0s
  
  • Let me look at the main parser setup and how the package is named.
  
    read_file · 1 call · 0s
  
  • Let me check the package metadata and any existing version handling/tests.
  
    read_file · grep · 2 calls · 0s
  
  • The codebase is clear. The package is named imp (version 0.0.1 in
    pyproject.toml), and the CLI is a single argparse parser in
    src/imp/cli/main.py with required=True subparsers.
  
    Here's my proposed design:
  
     • Add parser.add_argument("--version", "-V", action="version",
       version=f"imp {<version>}") to the top-level parser in main(). Argparse's
       version action fires during parse_args and exits 0 before the
       required-subparser check, so imp --version / imp -V work with no
       subcommand — no special-casing needed.
     • Read the version via a small helper using
       importlib.metadata.version("imp").
     • Output format: imp 0.0.1 (one line, to stdout, exit 0) — the argparse
       version action default.
     • Add a CLI test asserting imp --version and imp -V print the metadata
       version and exit 0.
  
    One decision worth your call: if the package metadata can't be found
    (PackageNotFoundError — e.g. running from a source checkout that was never
    installed), should --version (a) print a fallback like imp unknown and still
    exit 0, or (b) let it error out? I lean toward (a) so --version never
    crashes.
  
    Does this look right, and which fallback do you want?
  
  > Design looks right. Go with (a): on PackageNotFoundError, print `imp
    unknown` and still exit 0 so --version never crashes. Please also assert
    that fallback path in the test.
  
  • Naming this add-version-flag.
  
    rename_change · write_file · bash · complete_step · 4 calls · 22s
  
  • Spec written and committed as imp/specs/2026-06-06-add-version-flag.md. It
    captures the top-level --version/-V flag, version resolution via
    importlib.metadata.version("imp"), the imp unknown fallback on
    PackageNotFoundError (still exit 0), and tests covering both the success and
    fallback paths.

  • Strengths
  
     • Implementation satisfies the core spec: src/imp/cli/main.py imports
       importlib.metadata, adds _resolve_version() that calls
       importlib.metadata.version("imp") at call time, and falls back to
       "unknown" on PackageNotFoundError.
     • The version flag is wired on the top-level parser only, before
       add_subparsers(required=True), using argparse's action="version" with
       output format imp <version>. This allows imp --version and imp -V to exit
       0 without a subcommand.
     • The diff is tightly scoped to src/imp/cli/main.py and
       tests/test_cli_version.py; pyproject.toml remains unchanged.
     • Tests cover the helper success/fallback paths and CLI behavior for
       --version, -V, and metadata-missing fallback. I spot-checked python -m
       pytest tests/test_cli_version.py -q, python -m ruff check
       src/imp/cli/main.py tests/test_cli_version.py, and python -m mypy
       src/imp/cli/main.py tests/test_cli_version.py; all passed.
  
    Issues
  
    Critical (Must Fix)
  
    None.
  
    Important (Should Fix)
  
    None.
  
    Minor / Nit
  
     • Existing carried followup remains:
       test_resolve_version_reads_package_metadata and the CLI success tests
       patch importlib.metadata.version with lambdas that ignore the dist
       argument. The implementation correctly uses "imp", so this is not
       blocking, but asserting dist == "imp" in the fake would make the tests
       catch wrong-distribution regressions more directly.
     • Existing carried followup remains: _resolve_version() is evaluated when
       main() builds the parser, even for non-version invocations. This is
       acceptable for a small CLI metadata lookup and keeps the code simple.
  
    Verdict
  
    approve — the implementation meets the acceptance criteria, is well scoped,
    and the behavior is covered by passing tests.

    Task 1 — Version-resolution helper (SHA 0b30278, "feat: add _resolve_version
    helper for imp --version"): added a module-level _resolve_version() to
    src/imp/cli/main.py that reads importlib.metadata.version("imp") at call
    time (with a new import importlib.metadata) so the printed version stays in
    sync with packaged metadata, and returns "unknown" on PackageNotFoundError

    patchable in tests. Created tests/test_cli_version.py with two unit tests
    covering the success and fallback paths.

    add --version/-V flag to imp CLI top-level parser"): added

    {_resolve_version()}") to the top-level argparse parser in main(), placed
    before add_subparsers(..., required=True). argparse's version action fires
    during parse_args and exits 0 before the required-subparser check, so imp
    --version / imp -V work with no subcommand. Appended three CLI tests to
    tests/test_cli_version.py asserting the printed line and exit-0 for the long
    flag, the short flag, and the fallback. No subparser or pyproject.toml

  final-review · sonnet
  
    ToolSearch · query_events · 2 calls · 2s
  
  • Change Summary: 2026-06-06-add-version-flag
  
    What was built
  
    A --version / -V flag was added to the top-level imp CLI, delivered in two
    commits:
  
    Task 1 — _resolve_version() helper (SHA 0b30278)
  
     • Added import importlib.metadata and a new _resolve_version() function to
       src/imp/cli/main.py.
     • The function reads importlib.metadata.version("imp") at call time, so the
       version stays in sync with the installed package metadata.
     • Falls back to "unknown" on PackageNotFoundError (e.g., uninstalled source
       checkout) — no crash.
     • Created tests/test_cli_version.py with 2 unit tests covering success and
       fallback paths.
  
    Task 2 — Wire the flag (HEAD 5db7b46)
  
     • Added parser.add_argument("--version", "-V", action="version",
       version=f"imp {_resolve_version()}") to the top-level argparse parser in
       main(), placed before add_subparsers(..., required=True).
     • argparse's version action fires during parse_args and exits 0 before the
       required-subparser check fires — so imp --version and imp -V work even
       with no subcommand.
     • 3 additional CLI integration tests added: long flag, short flag, and
       metadata-missing fallback.
     • pyproject.toml and all subparsers are untouched.
  
    Test status ✅
  
     • pytest tests/test_cli_version.py -q → 5 passed
     • ruff check → all checks passed
     • mypy → no issues found
     • Smoke test: imp --version and imp -V both print imp 0.0.1 and exit 0.
  
    Open (non-blocking) items
  
     • Minor: The helper unit test uses lambda dist: "9.9.9-test" without
       asserting dist == "imp" — a tweak that would catch wrong-package-name
       regressions.
     • Nit: _resolve_version() is called eagerly on every main() invocation
       (harmless for a short-lived CLI process).
  
    ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  
    All 7 acceptance criteria are satisfied. The code reviewer gave an approve
